{{short description|Spanish politician}}
'''Luis María Bandrés''' ([[Basque language|Basque]]: '''Luis Mari Bandrés''') (18 February 1944 [[Pasaia]] - 2 December 2009) was a Spanish politician who served as the leader of the [[Basque Nationalist Party]] (PNV).<ref name=elpais>{{cite news |title=Fallece Luis María Bandrés |url=https://www.elpais.com/articulo/espana/Fallece/Luis/Maria/Bandres/elpepuespvas/20091203elpepunac_28/Tes |work=[[El País]] |date=2009-12-03 |access-date=2009-12-27}}</ref>

Bandrés was born on 18 February 1944 and was a native of [[Pasaia]], [[Guipúzcoa]].<ref name=elpais/> He worked as a professor at the [[la Escuela Universitaria de Ingenieros Técnicos Industriales]] in [[San Sebastián]] from 1965 until 1969.<ref name=elpais/>

Bandrés was described as a [[Basque nationalist]].<ref name=elpais/> He served as the Minister of Culture within the Basque government of [[José María Ardanza]], as well as the Guipúzcoa Provincial Council.<ref name=elpais/> He became a Basque parliamentarian as a member of the [[Basque Nationalist Party]] and the party's executive leader in Guipúzcoa.<ref name=elpais/> He later became the leader of the Basque National Party (PNV) and continued to serve in that capacity until his death in 2009.<ref name=elpais/>

Luis María Bandrés died on 2 December 2009 after a long illness, at the age of 65.<ref name=elpais/> His funeral was held at Santa María [[parish]] in [[San Sebastián|San Sebastian]].<ref name=elpais/>
